_readme: State outlines for the region gate. buildplaces uses these to tell 'this point stands in a state we do not map' from 'this point is over water', which is the difference between another state's park and one of our own islands — the municipality snap alone cannot tell them apart, because both are 'outside every town polygon and nearby'.
_source: US Census TIGERweb State_County MapServer layer 0, fetched 2026-08-13
_simplify: 0.0005 degrees, about 50 m. Coarser tolerances move the NY/NJ line far enough to put Sterling Forest State Park, which is 2 m inside it, on the wrong side.
